title: Fastest Jet Ski Models in 2025: Ranked by Speed and Performance
summary: Discover the fastest jet ski models of 2025, ranked by speed, power, and performance. Compare top PWCs and find your perfect ride for the open water
body_text: Back Fastest Jet Ski Models in 2025: Ranked by Speed and Performance Aug. 14 2025 Adventure By RideNow jetski water sports Share Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Email to a Friend Speed. Power. Open water. That’s what 2025’s top jet skis are all about. If you’ve got a need for speed and want to know which machines actually deliver, you’re in the right place. This year’s fastest PWC models are built to dominate the waves with raw performance and tight control. Let’s kick things off by talking about why speed on the water makes all the difference. Why Speed Matters in Jet Skis Speed is what separates the average ride from an all-out experience. When you’re ripping across the water at 65+ mph, it’s not just a rush. It’s freedom. Faster jet skis give you the ability to cover more distance, carve harder turns, and take on tougher water conditions with confidence. Whether you’re racing buddies, jumping wakes, or just eating up miles on a big lake, more speed means more fun—and more control when it counts. But it’s not just about going full throttle. High-speed models usually come with better handling, tighter hull designs, and more responsive throttles. You’re getting sharper, smoother performance across the board. Think of speed as the starting point. The real question is: how much power can you handle? Key Performance Factors That Impact Jet Ski Speed Speed on a personal watercraft comes down to more than engine size. If you’re looking to go fast, you’ve got to look under the hood (and the hull). The engine’s the obvious piece: more horsepower equals more top-end speed. Most high-performance models in 2025 are pushing well past 300 horsepower, and some are creeping close to 400. That’s superbike territory, just on water. But speed isn’t just about brute force. Hull design matters—a lot. A deep-V hull slices through chop better and gives you more stability at high speeds. Lightweight materials like fiberglass-reinforced composites can cut down drag and help you accelerate faster. A solid power-to-weight ratio—including dry weight—is critical. Lighter frames, like those using carbon fiber components, give a serious edge in acceleration. Then there’s tech. Some models come speed-governed out of the box but can be unlocked with tuning kits or racing keys. And don’t forget rider load—every extra pound slows you down. Bottom line: the fastest skis balance power, precision, and weight. Miss one, and you’re leaving speed on the table. 🥇 1. Kawasaki Jet Ski® Ultra® 310 Top Speed: ~67 mph (stock, ECU-limited) Engine: Supercharged 1,498cc inline-four, 310 hp Why it dominates: The Ultra 310 is a powerhouse wrapped in premium design. Known for its supercharged performance and heavy-duty hull, it crushes waves and handles like a champ. Add in its large fuel tank and touring-friendly features, and you’ve got a machine that does it all. Pros: Supercharged power and torque Stable in rough water Loaded with tech (launch control, 7" display, reverse braking) Cons: Heavy compared to sportier models Price tag reflects its premium features 🥈 2. Yamaha GP SVHO Top Speed: ~67–68 mph Engine: Supercharged 1.8L (~250 hp) Why it’s a top contender: Built for closed-course dominance, the GP SVHO is lightweight, sharp in the corners, and dialed in for aggressive riding. It’s a racer’s favorite for a reason. Pros: Lightning-fast response Nimble and agile Great aftermarket support Cons: Rougher ride in choppy water Fewer comfort features than touring models 🥉 3. Sea-Doo RXP-X 325 Top Speed: ~68 mph Engine: 325 hp Rotax 1630 ACE Why it stands out: Sea-Doo’s newest race weapon brings explosive holeshots, aggressive cornering, and digital ride modes that fine-tune every session. It’s built to win. Pros: Launch control for brutal starts Deep-V hull grips like crazy Customizable ride settings Cons: Not ideal for beginners Less plush than touring skis 4. Yamaha FX SVHO Top Speed: ~67 mph Engine: Supercharged 1.8L (~250 hp) Standout traits: The FX SVHO balances muscle and luxury. With tons of storage, a stable hull, and touchscreen tech, it's perfect for long, fast rides with a little more comfort. Pros: Long-distance touring meets speed Stable, confidence-inspiring hull Smooth ride for passengers Cons: Heavier than race models Slightly slower off the line 5. Sea-Doo GTX Limited 300 Top Speed: ~65–66 mph Engine: 300 hp Rotax engine Why it’s here: Want sports-level speed and a lounge chair vibe? The GTX Limited 300 brings the best of both. Long fuel range, plush seating, and tech for days. Pros: Rider-friendly and super stable Massive fuel capacity for all-day runs Cruise control + sound system Cons: Not as nimble as sportier models More cruise, less carve How to Choose the Right Fast Jet Ski for You If you're just getting into high-performance skis, don’t jump straight into the most extreme model. Something like the Yamaha GP 320SS or Sea-Doo GTX-R 300 gives you serious speed with a little more forgiveness. You’ll still feel the rush, just without getting tossed the first time you hammer the throttle. More experienced riders? Go big. The Ultra 400X or RXP-X 350 were built for power junkies who know how to handle it. You’ll appreciate the sharper handling, stronger acceleration, and tuning flexibility. Also think about where you’re riding. Choppy lakes, open ocean, calm rivers—each terrain rewards different hull designs and features. And if you’re planning long days on the water, don’t ignore comfort: seat design, storage, and ride stability all come into play. Fast isn’t one-size-fits-all. Match your machine to your experience, your water, and your goals—and the speed will take care of itself. Maintenance and Safety Tips for High-Speed Jet Skis Fast skis need more than just gas. They need respect. High-performance watercrafts put stress on every part: the engine, the impeller, the hull. Skip the upkeep, and you’ll go from 70 mph to stuck-on-the-dock real quick. First rule? Stick to the maintenance schedule. Oil changes, coolant flushes, and supercharger checks aren’t optional—they’re your ticket to keeping that power dialed in. Pushing 300+ hp through a lightweight frame takes a toll, and systems like SVHO propulsion need attention. Launch control modules and advanced handlebars also need calibration over time. Second, inspect your jet pump and impeller regularly. These parts take a beating at high speeds and need to be clean and damage-free to keep your acceleration crisp. Now, let’s talk safety. Fast jet skis demand full attention. Wear a properly fitted life vest, use a kill switch lanyard every time, and don’t ride without checking conditions. Even pros can get surprised by chop or debris at high speeds. Want to stay fast? Keep your gear tight, your machine clean, and your head in the game. Rule the Water in 2025 When it comes to speed on the water, 2025 is delivering some absolute monsters. Ready to ride one for yourself? Shop the fastest 2025 jet skis now at RideNow Powersports —huge selection, expert advice, and nationwide delivery available.

title: Sypris Reports Second Quarter Results
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Sypris Solutions, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: PDF Version Orders Up 110% To $47 Million For Sypris Electronics Strong Demand From Electronic Warfare And Communications Markets LOUISVILLE, Ky.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 12, 2025-- Sypris Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq/GM: SYPR) today reported financial results for its second quarter ended June 29, 2025. HIGHLIGHTS ────────────────────────────────── The Company’s second quarter revenue decreased compared to the prior-year quarter primarily due to the near-term impact of tariffs, which reduced demand from certain transportation-related customers and necessitated the conversion of certain shipments from our facility in Mexico to a value-add only sub-maquiladora. The Company’s gross profit decreased compared to the prior-year period due to the volume decrease described above, an unfavorable mix for both segments, and production inefficiencies resulting from material availability issues for Sypris Electronics. Orders for Sypris Electronics increased 110% to $47 million, driving backlog up 26% from year-end 2024. Orders for our energy products increased slightly when compared to the prior-year quarter, while backlog rose 26% from year-end 2024. During the quarter, Sypris Electronics announced a follow-on award from a U.S. DoD prime contractor for a secure communications infrastructure program. Sypris will manufacture and test the embedded circuit card assemblies that will perform certain cryptographic functions for the Army Key Management System. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2026. Sypris Electronics also announced that it received releases for an additional four systems under a multi-year production contract that was first announced in 2022. The modules to be produced by Sypris will be integrated into an electronic warfare improvement program for the U.S. Navy. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2026. Sypris Technologies announced that it entered a long-term agreement to supply certain drivetrain components for a new electrified truck of a leading global commercial vehicle manufacturer. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2026. Subsequent to quarter end, Sypris Electronics announced that it had secured follow-on contract awards to manufacture and test electronic power supply modules for multiple high-reliability subsea communication networks, with production currently underway and expected to continue through 2026. ────────────────────────────────── “The past few months have been insightful as we evaluate how tariffs might affect the economy and our customers, which may, in turn, affect our overall results,” commented Jeffrey T. Gill, President and Chief Executive Officer. “We are focused on operational excellence to drive the timely and efficient execution of the rapidly growing demand at Sypris Electronics. Customer funding has already been secured for a portion of the key programs, which enables us to procure inventory under multi-year purchase orders to mitigate future supply chain issues. “A moderate decrease in production is anticipated this year from Sypris Technologies customers in the automotive, commercial vehicle, sport-utility and off-highway markets. However, we believe that the market diversification Sypris Technologies has accomplished over recent years by adding new programs in the automotive, sport-utility and off-highway markets will help offset some of the anticipated cyclical decline for the commercial vehicle market. “Orders for our energy products remained steady during the period, with open quotes still outstanding on several large projects. Additional opportunities for growth may exist with new global projects in support of increasing LNG demand, including support for the projected steep increase in electricity demand from data centers to support AI. We are also actively pursuing applications for our products in adjacent markets including CO2 capture to further diversify our industry and customer portfolios.” Second Quarter Results The Company reported revenue of $31.4 million for the second quarter of 2025, compared to $35.5 million for the prior-year comparable period. Additionally, the Company reported a net loss of $2.1 million, or $0.09 per share, compared with breakeven net income for the prior-year period. For the six months ended June 29, 2025, the Company reported revenue of $60.9 million compared to $71.1 million for the first half of 2024. The Company reported a net loss of $3.0 million compared with a net loss of $2.2 million for the prior-year period. Sypris Technologies Revenue for Sypris Technologies was $14.1 million in the second quarter of 2025 compared to $17.8 million for the prior-year period, reflecting the anticipated cyclical decline in the commercial vehicle market in addition to volume declines related to tariff uncertainty. Furthermore, during 2025, Sypris Technologies began operating under a sub-maquiladora services agreement with one of its customers in Mexico under which the material is consigned to us by the customer instead of being included in the price. This resulted in a revenue decrease of $1.6 million as compared to the prior-year comparable period. Gross profit for the second quarter of 2025 was $2.1 million, or 15.2% of revenue, compared to $2.7 million, or 15.2% of revenue, for the same period in 2024. Gross profit for the second quarter of 2025 was negatively impacted by the decrease in volumes, partially offset by a $0.4 million favorable impact from foreign currency exchange rates for our Mexican subsidiary. Sypris Electronics Revenue for Sypris Electronics was $17.3 million in the second quarter of 2025 compared to $17.7 million for the prior-year period as a result of changes in customer delivery schedules for the current year and delays resulting from material availability issues. Gross profit for the second quarter of 2025 was $0.4 million, or 2.5% of revenue, compared to $2.9 million, or 16.5% of revenue, for the same period in 2024. Some of the material availability issues have delayed certain customer deliveries, limited our ability to ramp up production in response to customer demand for certain products and have caused out-of-sequence manufacturing, which increases costs and decreases operational efficiency. Outlook Commenting on the future, Mr. Gill added, “With a strong backlog, new program wins and long-term contract extensions in place, we are confident that our future has the potential to be very positive despite the increased market uncertainty. We are closely monitoring customer demand and forward-looking signals and believe our long-standing track record of resilience will allow us to successfully navigate any headwinds. While we anticipate a modest decline in revenue due to the conversion of certain shipments from Mexico to the U.S. into a value-add only sub-maquiladora basis, and the cyclical decrease in production volumes in the commercial vehicle market, we expect the combined strength of our backlog for Sypris Electronics and robust orders for our energy products to serve as a partial offset.” About Sypris Solutions Sypris Solutions is a diversified manufacturing and engineering services company serving the defense, transportation, communications, and energy industries. For more information about Sypris Solutions, visit its Web site at www.sypris.com . title: Financing a Motorcycle: Everything You Need to Know Before You Buy
summary: Learn how to finance a motorcycle with tips on loans, rates, lenders, and pre-approval to save money and ride off with confidence.
body_text: Back Financing a Motorcycle: Everything You Need to Know Before You Buy Aug. 14 2025 Informative By RideNow motorcycle Financing Share Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Email to a Friend There’s nothing like the thrill of hitting the open road on your own bike. The wind in your face, the engine rumbling beneath you, it’s pure freedom. But before you rev the engine and speed off into the sunset, there's one important step to take: figuring out your motorcycle financing. If you're looking at a Harley-Davidson cruiser , a Yamaha bike , or an off-road ATV , understanding your financing options can save you time, money, and a whole lot of stress. Let’s break it down in simple terms, so even if it’s your first time buying a motorcycle, you’ll know exactly what to expect. What Is Motorcycle Financing? Motorcycle financing means borrowing money to buy a new or used motorcycle. It usually involves getting a motorcycle loan from a lender like a bank, credit union, dealership, or online lenders. You'll make monthly payments until the loan is paid off. Just like with a car, you’ll sign a loan agreement that includes the loan amount, interest rate, repayment terms, and disclosures. A loan application is usually required, and the lender will check your credit score and credit history. If you're wondering how much you'll be paying each month, a motorcycle loan calculator is a great place to start. It lets you plug in numbers for the loan amount, interest rate, and loan terms to see your estimated monthly payments. New Motorcycle vs. Used Motorcycle Financing Financing a new motorcycle often comes with lower interest rates and better warranty options. Dealerships may even offer promotional loan offers for first-time buyers or buyers with good credit. Some even include flexible terms or zero-interest periods. Used motorcycle loans can still be a great deal, especially if you're looking to lower your upfront cost. However, they may come with higher interest rates, shorter loan terms, and less warranty coverage. Make sure to compare loan options and calculate the total cost of ownership, including things like maintenance, insurance, and registration. What Affects Motorcycle Loan Rates? Several factors determine your motorcycle loan rate: Credit score : A good credit score can help you get the lowest rates. A low score may mean higher interest rates. Loan amount: Bigger loans can offer more competitive rates, but you’ll owe more in total. Down payment: A larger down payment reduces the amount you borrow, which can lead to lower interest costs. Loan terms: Shorter loan terms usually mean higher monthly payments but less interest overall. Longer terms may offer lower payments but can result in more interest paid over time. Type of loan: Secured loans typically have lower rates than unsecured loans, like a personal loan. Lenders and Loan Options You’ve got choices when it comes to lenders: Dealership financing : This is often the easiest route. Dealers sometimes offer special motorcycle financing deals, especially on models like Harley-Davidson or Yamaha. Just make sure to read the fine print. Banks and credit unions: Credit unions often have more competitive rates and may be more flexible with approval. Online lenders: These can offer fast approval and a wide range of options, but always check the disclosures and compare offers. Personal loan: This is an unsecured loan you can use for any purpose, including buying a motorcycle. Since there’s no collateral, you may see higher interest rates. It’s smart to shop around and compare lenders. Look for the best motorcycle loan with low rates, flexible terms, and no hidden fees. Pre-Approval: Why It Matters Getting pre-approval for a motorcycle loan before visiting the dealership gives you a big advantage. It helps you: Know your budget Understand your loan options Compare offers easily Speed up the buying process Once you’re pre-approved, you can focus on finding the right bike without worrying about the financing part. It also helps you negotiate better loan terms because you’re already an informed borrower. Understanding Loan Types: Secured vs. Unsecured Loans Most motorcycle loans are secured loans, which means the bike acts as collateral. If you don't make your payments, the lender can take the motorcycle. Personal loans are unsecured loans, meaning there's no collateral. These might be useful if you're buying from a private seller, but the downside is higher interest rates and shorter repayment terms. Knowing the difference can help you pick the right loan for your situation. Refinancing and Loan Payment Flexibility Already have a motorcycle loan? You may want to consider refinancing. This can help you: Lock in a lower interest rate Extend your loan terms Reduce your monthly payment Refinancing is especially helpful if your credit score has improved or if you've found better loan offers with more competitive rates. Just remember to compare the total cost, including fees and any changes in the annual percentage rate. Tips for First-Time Borrowers Buying your first bike? Keep these tips in mind: Check your credit report for errors before applying Improve your credit score if possible like pay down debt, make payments on time Compare financing options from multiple lenders Budget for extras like registration, safety gear, and insurance Understand your loan terms before signing anything Being prepared makes the process smoother and helps you avoid surprises. Warranty and Extra Costs A warranty can save you big money on repairs, especially with a new motorcycle. Some dealerships let you roll the cost of the warranty into your financing, which can help reduce upfront expenses. Just know this may increase your monthly loan payment slightly. Be sure to read the warranty details carefully. Know what’s covered, what isn’t, and how long the coverage lasts. FAQs: Quick Answers to Common Questions Can I finance a motorcycle with bad credit? Yes, but expect higher interest rates. A co-signer or a larger down payment can help improve your chances. Is a credit card a good way to buy a motorcycle? Not usually. Unless you can pay it off quickly, a motorcycle loan will typically offer lower interest rates. Do I need insurance before I finance a bike? Yes. Most lenders require proof of insurance before finalizing the loan. What if I want to pay off early? Many loans allow early payoff without penalties, but always check your loan disclosures. What’s the benefit of a fixed-rate loan? Fixed-rate loans mean your interest rate and monthly payments stay the same over time, making budgeting easier. Final Thoughts Financing a motorcycle doesn’t have to be overwhelming. With the right information and tools, like a motorcycle loan calculator and a clear understanding of your loan options, you can find the best motorcycle loan for your needs. RideNow has financing options that work for your lifestyle. From low rates to flexible repayment terms, we’re here to help. Contact us today or visit your local RideNow dealership .

title: Stuck in the end-of-summer slump? Here’s how to rebuild your momentum.
summary: Learn what causes the end-of-summer slump and how you can regain your momentum as we head into a new season.
body_text: The end-of-summer slump is real. You’re saying goodbye to all of the joy that summer had to offer, but you haven’t yet shifted into high gear for a productive fall. The result is this weird middle place where you know it’s time to jump into action, and your mind is ready to do so, but you can’t quite figure out how to get started. Let’s talk through what needs to happen next so you can escape the slump and make plans for a productive autumn. Why your brain struggles after summer The data is in: you’re not the only one feeling unproductive. Productivity drops by 20% over the summer, and workers struggle with distractions and post-vacation blues when they’re in the office. Understanding the reasons behind this slump can help you approach your recovery with more self-compassion and strategic thinking. We’re implementing more structure after 3 months of flexibility Almost my entire life has been shaped by the school calendar—first as a student, then as a teacher, and now as a parent. I assumed that having a tie to this type of schedule is what made summer feel different for me, until a conversation I recently had with my sister, who works in the medical field and has no children. She commented that she and her husband were ready to do absolutely nothing outside of work for the next few weeks, because their summer had been so packed and busy. Structure tends to disappear during summer, regardless of your life stage. It’s not just about kids or school; it’s about how our culture treats summer as a break, which means both our personal and professional priorities shift. Even if you no longer have a direct tie to the academic calendar, other people you work with might. Colleagues take vacations, clients take longer to answer, and business moves at a slower pace. We’re emotionally resistant to change The end of summer can bring feelings of loss. You know you won’t have the same freedom, flexibility, and fun that accompanied the summer months. Even if you’re craving routine again, there’s often a small part of you that’s still dreaming about the open feeling of summer. This emotional resistance can create some internal stress and might even cause some premature burnout. Sarah Whitman, the senior vice-president of e-commerce at Workhuman, describes it this way: “There’s a sense of anticipation and worry that all the fun is over, and there are only challenges ahead—it’s almost like those back-to-school blues that came up when we were kids.” Your grief is legitimate. Summer can be a time when you feel most like yourself, more relaxed, more social, and more spontaneous. The transition back to structured productivity can be uncomfortable, especially if your company is rolling out any RTO mandates. Recognizing this emotional factor is crucial because it means your resistance is a normal psychological response to change. The summer drop in productivity might make you feel lazy, especially when you come across headlines like Summer slackers are plaguing bosses everywhere . The truth is that summer provides a different work environment from the other three seasons, and when we are willing to recognize that, we’re better equipped to accept the lower productivity of summer while we anticipate how to jump back into our efforts during the fall. Here’s how to get the ball rolling. Track your time to understand your patterns Before you rebuild your momentum, it helps to understand how you’ve been spending your time. With this information, you can make a plan to help you move forward. Go into this data collection as objectively as you can— no judging yourself! How to analyze your last 30 days Memory is a fickle thing and is easily manipulated based on what we want to think happened. If you want an accurate representation of how you spent your working hours over the past month, you need to lean into the data. RescueTime reports are an easy way to evaluate the last 30 days, and there are a number of insights you can discover about how you’ve been spending your time. Below are just a few: Which days of the week are most productive To get started, head to Productivity → Reports → Productivity . From here, look for the date picker on the upper-left side of the report, then select Last 30 days . Filter your productivity reports By Day to see which days you’ve been able to stay focused and which days were more of a wash. What time of day is most productive Filter your results by Time of Day to see when most of your focus work is taking place. This information is golden as you rebuild your schedule because it reveals your natural energy patterns. A routine built around your natural rhythms will feel less forced and more sustainable. How long projects truly take Open your Apps and Websites report and you’ll see a detailed breakdown of where your time actually goes. When you scroll down, you can see the exact amount of time you spent in certain documents. For me, this helps me compare how long pieces take to write vs. how long I think I spent writing them. Talk about a reality check. How much you’re working outside of your designated work hours Head over to Productivity → Focus & Balance → Balance . Here, you can access reports to see if/when you’re working outside of the boundaries you’ve set, including exactly how much time you’re working during your after-work time. For example, you might discover that the summer slump you’re feeling isn’t because you had poor productivity, but because you didn’t rest enough. How much time you’re spending on communication Go to Productivity → Focus & Balance → Communication . You can see: How much time you spend in various communication apps. How frequently you check email and chat Which tools you use most often Understanding your communication patterns helps identify whether constant connectivity is fragmenting your focus. Summer’s more relaxed pace might have allowed for more scattered communication habits that are now keeping you from deep work Common time audit discoveries Whether you use RescueTime, another time-tracking software, or a pencil-and-paper time audit, you’ll probably find at least one of these patterns. You’re spending way too much time on low-value tasks. Busy ≠ productive. A time audit helps you see if you’re stuck in low-value tasks or having your calendar overrun with unnecessary meetings. Summer’s relaxed pace can make it easier to get caught up in busy work, and if that’s the case for you, it’s time to check your priorities. You’re underestimating task duration. Having a clear idea of how much time a task takes is a game-changer. When something takes 2-3 times longer than you anticipated, you know it’s time to rearrange your schedule or consider how you can become more efficient. You have more free time than you think. But it’s fragmented 😬 Maybe you don’t have any long stretches of uninterrupted time, but your schedule is full of scattered 10-20 minute blocks. You need to determine how you’re going to use those blocks or rework your schedule for longer stretches of free time. You’re not getting enough restorative time. Small, scattered portions of free time usually won’t do enough to restore your soul. And if your relaxing time isn’t restful (i.e., you spend it all doomscrolling), you probably never feel fully rested. Learn what your procrastination means Just as important as how you spent your time is the data about how you didn’t spend your time. Are there certain apps or projects you should have spent more time using? That information reveals patterns about your avoidance behaviors. Why are you putting off certain tasks? Are you not sure about the expectations? Feeling overwhelmed? Just don’t want to do it? Getting to the reason behind your procrastination helps you determine the right solution, because different types of procrastination require different approaches. Design your day with intention Once you know what’s been working and what hasn’t, you have the information you need to build something better. Go from data → insights → action Let’s start with all the juicy data you got from your time audit. We already listed specific insights you can glean from each data point, so let’s talk about how you can turn those insights into actionable steps. If you see a certain activity spiking when you’d like to limit it, set up an alert to give yourself a little nudge when you want to get things back under control. If you’re having trouble staying focused for long periods of time, schedule Focus Sessions that incrementally grow in length as you retrain your brain. If you notice your energy dips at the same time every day, reserve that time for low-value tasks that don’t require much focus. If communication apps are eating away at your time, set specific windows for checking messages and mute notifications. Move beyond simple habit changes I’m all for habit stacking—it’s a great way to sneak new routines into your workday without overhauling everything. But those habits won’t last unless you know exactly why you’re doing them. For example, adding a five-minute inbox clean-up right after your afternoon coffee break might work for a while, but it’ll fizzle if you don’t tackle the stress that makes you avoid your inbox in the first place. Set specific goals + make a plan to reach them Our attention tends to drift when our goals get vague– the brain needs clarity to focus effectively. When you set vague goals (like be more productive or get in shape ), your brain struggles to identify what success looks like and what steps need to be taken. Without clear parameters, your attention drifts toward easier, more concrete tasks that give you a quick reward. There’s also a heavy cognitive load that comes with being vague or open-ended about what you want to accomplish. I’ve lived in the same town my entire life, so getting from place to place is never really an issue, unless I know there are 3 or 4 possible routes I could take . When that happens, I end up sitting there and weighing out my options, comparing each route, trying to decide which way I want to go instead of just driving. When you don’t have a specific plan to get from A to B, you end up spending a lot of time and energy thinking about what needs to happen next, instead of just taking action. I’m sorry to sound like your fifth-grade guidance counselor, but there’s a reason that SMART goals are recommended time and again. Creating specific, measurable, time-bound goals is half the battle when you need a plan of action. The other half? Breaking those goals into clear, bite-sized steps so you always know your next move. That way, you reduce decision fatigue, keep momentum going, and make it far more likely you’ll reach the finish line. Build structure that flexes with you A too-rigid schedule can sometimes slow you down. It often doesn’t account for energy fluctuations and ignores real-life interruptions, meaning that one small hiccup can send you spiraling for the rest of the day. Instead of planning your day with military precision, create a general framework that guides you through the day. Block your time in themes like creative work, admin tasks, and meetings. Build in buffer zones for overflow or recovery, giving yourself some transition time between tasks. Set anchor points to guide your day, such as starting around 9 am and eating lunch around 12. Keep a running list of low-pressure tasks (like decluttering digital files or clearing out your inbox) that you can do when your energy dips or you have one of those fragments of free time. Takeaway The end-of-summer slump doesn’t have to define your entire fall. By understanding why it happens, auditing your current patterns, and building a structure that works with your natural rhythm, you can create sustainable momentum that carries you through the rest of the year.

title: How Much Does Exterior Trim Installation Cost? [2026 Data] | Angi
summary: Discover the cost to install exterior trim. Learn about price factors, labor, materials, and ways to save on your exterior trim installation project.
body_text:
Written by Mitchell Grant Contributing Writer Reviewed by Morgan Rousseau Editor Updated May 30, 2026 Cost Insights: Professional exterior trim installation ranges from $500 to $9,000 , with most homeowners paying around $1,800 for your complete project. Your trim material choice and your home's architectural details determine the complexity and labor hours needed for proper installation. Hiring a local siding professional prevents water damage and ensures your trim withstands harsh weather for years. The cost to install exterior trim ranges from $500 to $9,000 , with an average project costing $1,800 . Homeowners can expect to pay between $6 and $15 per linear foot, depending on the trim material and project size. Larger homes or custom trim profiles may increase the total price. Exterior trim not only frames your home’s style but also shields it from the elements. This guide will walk you through the factors that affect the cost to install exterior trim, how to plan your project, and what to expect every step of the way. Cost by Size of Exterior Trim Project The overall size and scope of your exterior trim project play a major role in determining your total cost. The more linear feet of trim you need, the higher your material and labor expenses will be. For smaller homes, trim installation might cover the basic perimeter and a few windows and doors, while larger or multi-story homes require significantly more footage. Complex architectural features, such as bay windows, dormers, or wraparound porches, increase the amount of trim required. The number of windows, doors, and corners on your home also directly affects the amount of trim you’ll need. Choosing to install trim on the entire exterior versus just a section—like a front façade—will also change your project’s price. Home Size/Project Scope Lin. Ft. of Trim Average Cost Small home/partial facade 100–150 $600–$2,250 Medium home/full trim 200–300 $1,200–$4,500 Large home/complex features 400–600 $2,400–$9,000 Exterior Trim Cost by Type The type of exterior trim you select has a significant impact on cost, appearance, and durability. Common trim types include fascia boards (which cover the roof edge), soffits (under the eaves), window and door casings, corner boards, and decorative moldings. Each serves a different purpose and varies in installation complexity. Standard trim profiles are more budget-friendly, while custom millwork or ornate details will increase both material and labor costs. The right trim type depends on your home’s style, climate, and your maintenance preferences. Trim Type Cost per Lin. Ft. Pros Cons Fascia $6–$12 Essential for gutters, clean look Prone to water damage if wood Soffit $4–$10 Ventilation, protects rafters Can be hard to access Window/door casing $5–$15 Boosts curb appeal, seals gaps Custom shapes cost more Corner boards $6–$14 Protects corners, accent detail May require custom fitting Decorative molding $10–$25 Unique look, boosts value Higher labor, upkeep Exterior Trim Cost by Location Where you live can affect the cost to install exterior trim, due to differences in labor rates, material availability, and local codes. Urban areas often have higher labor costs than rural locations. Climate also plays a role; homes in wet or coastal areas may require premium, weather-resistant materials. Some cities or regions require permits for exterior trim work, which can add to your total cost. Exterior Trim Installation Cost Factors Several factors influence the cost to install exterior trim. Understanding these can help you plan and budget effectively. Labor The professionals who install exterior trim range from skilled carpenters and general contractors to siding specialists. Labor is charged by the hour, per linear foot, or by the entire project. Hourly rates often fall between $40 and $90, while per-foot rates align with the complexity of the trim. Minimum service fees apply to small projects, making them relatively more expensive per foot. Labor costs increase for experienced specialists, multi-story homes, or hard-to-reach areas. Labor includes preparation, installation, caulking, and cleanup, but always confirm with your contractor. Permits Permits may be required for exterior trim installation, especially in areas with strict building codes or for historic homes. Permit costs vary by location, ranging from $50 to $300. Your contractor often handles permit applications, but it’s important to clarify responsibility up front. Permit requirements can impact your project’s timeline and budget, so plan accordingly. Additional Features Upgrading your trim with decorative moldings, crown details, or custom millwork can add style and value, but it also increases costs. Weatherproofing details—such as flashing, premium caulking, or advanced sealants—help protect your home but add to your materials bill. Painting or staining the trim after installation is another expense to consider. Some homeowners also opt for insulated trim or trim that integrates with gutters or siding for improved energy efficiency and protection. Installation Add-Ons There are several factors that influence total labor costs when installing exterior trim: Intricate profiles , curved or angled trim, and multi-story work increase complexity and cost. Accessibility challenges , such as steep roofs or dense landscaping, may require scaffolding or extra labor. Site preparation , including removing old trim, disposal fees, and delivery of new materials, can add to your budget. Post-construction cleanup and debris removal are sometimes charged separately. Design or architectural consultation fees may apply for custom projects. Inspections could be required by local codes or homeowner's associations. Additional Costs to Consider Beyond installation, there are ongoing and one-time costs to keep in mind for your exterior trim project. Warranties Exterior trim may come with manufacturer or installer warranties. Terms vary, but most cover defects or premature failure for five to 25 years. Extended warranties or service plans are sometimes available for an additional fee. Warranties can reduce long-term repair or replacement expenses, but always review the fine print for coverage limits and exclusions. Maintenance Maintenance requirements depend on your trim’s material. Wood trim needs more frequent painting and caulking, while PVC, fiber cement, and aluminum are lower-maintenance. Annual maintenance costs can range from $50 to $300, depending on your home’s size and the trim material. Watch for signs of wear, such as peeling paint or soft spots, to address problems early and extend trim lifespan. Taxes Sales tax on materials and labor varies by state and can add to your project total. If your trim installation is part of a major remodel, your property taxes could increase slightly due to a higher home value. Insurance Homeowner’s insurance may cover trim damage caused by storms or accidents, but not routine wear or neglect. Installing new trim does not increase insurance premiums, but always check your policy. Contractors should carry liability and workers’ compensation insurance during installation to protect you from risk. Why You Should Hire an Exterior Trim Installation Pro A local exterior trim pro will charge between $40 and $90 per hour in labor. Only DIYers with extensive, hands-on experience in this exact type of work should consider tackling it themselves. For most people, hiring a pro is the smarter choice to avoid errors and unexpected expenses. Here’s why it’s ideal to hire an exterior trim installation pro When you hire a pro, you’re not only paying for the hours they work on your project, but the years they spent mastering their craft. Some other reasons to hire a pro are: Pros understand trim materials, especially wood, better than homeowners. Trim undergoes a beating, and professionals know how to install it in order to withstand the elements. A proper installation prevents costly water damage to the home. If you are only doing a part of your home, a pro can match the new section to the old section. Having a second set of eyes on the integrity of your home is never a bad idea. Professionals will be familiar with the building codes and requirements for your area. If using wood, pros can arrange it to appear more cohesive by matching the wood’s grain direction. If you want to DIY an exterior trim installation There are some steps you can take to get the project set up for a pro (which we recommend). You can help by: Taking quality photos of the exterior of the entire home. Clear any landscaping or bushes that are in the way. Trim and tree limbs close to the house. If your pro gives the go-ahead, you can remove some existing pieces yourself. Inform your pro about any damage you may have noticed in the past, even if it was years ago. If you have an HOA, ensure that your new exterior trim adheres to their guidelines. Remove any window boxes, wasp nests, or other signs of animal life. Exterior Trim Replacement vs. Repair Deciding whether to repair or replace exterior trim depends on the extent of damage and the age of your trim. Minor issues, like small cracks, loose sections, or isolated rot, can often be repaired at a lower cost. Repairs might run $100 to $500, depending on the size and location. Full replacement is recommended when there’s widespread rot, water damage, or if your trim is outdated and no longer matches your home’s style. Replacing all exterior trim is costlier but provides a longer-term solution and can improve curb appeal. A good rule of thumb: If the cost to repair exceeds 50% of trim replacement costs , it’s best to replace. Assess the age and warranty status of your trim to help make your decision. Does Exterior Trim Add Value to Your Home? Installing new exterior trim offers a strong return on investment (ROI), often recouping 60% to 80% of its cost at resale. Fresh trim enhances curb appeal, making your home more attractive to buyers and improving first impressions. Compared to other exterior projects like siding or windows, trim is a relatively affordable upgrade with noticeable results. The quality of materials, design, color choice, and installation craftsmanship all influence your ROI. Besides value, new trim can improve weather resistance, energy efficiency, and overall safety while boosting your home’s visual character. Tips to Reduce Costs While Installing Exterior Trim Here are some helpful tips to keep exterior trim installation costs within budget: Get multiple quotes from licensed, insured contractors. Choose budget-friendly materials that offer durability and low maintenance. Limit custom profiles or ornate designs to reduce labor and material costs. Schedule installation during off-peak seasons for potential discounts. DIY prep or removal of old trim if safe and feasible. Bundle exterior trim installation with other exterior projects (e.g., siding, painting) for package pricing. Maintain trim regularly to avoid costly repairs or premature replacement. Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Pro Check to make sure your pro is recycling the material if it’s a requirement in your area. If you have wood trim, you may be able to repurpose it for other projects if it’s in good condition. Make sure disposal fees are marked in the quote. As you should for most professionals, verify that their insurance and licenses are current. title: The Ultimate Guide to Payroll: Preparation, Calculation, and Accounting in Africa
summary: payroll software Africa, cloud payroll software Africa, payroll processing, payroll management system Africa, automated payroll system Africa, employee self-service payroll, payroll outsourcing services, international/multi-country payroll, payroll compliance Africa, payroll accounting Africa
body_text: A Guide to Preparation, Calculation, and Accounting of Payroll in Africa Processing payroll is a critical function for any business, regardless of size or industry, serving as the lifeblood of a company that ensures financial and operational stability. It involves compensating employees for a specific period and on a particular date, encompassing tasks such as preparing payroll, calculating wages, and withholding taxes and other deductions. For businesses operating in Africa's rapidly growing landscape, understanding the intricacies of payroll, from preparation and calculation to accounting, is essential for sustainable scaling and maintaining employee morale. Understanding Payroll Basics Payroll is about more than just issuing pay slips and paychecks; it fosters trust, enhances loyalty between employers and employees, and ensures that everyone is paid correctly and on time. An effective and error-free payroll process is fundamental to a business's success. Why is Payroll Important? Compliance : Businesses must comply with tax regulations and labor laws, accurately paying employees and remitting all tax deductions to avoid fines and legal penalties. Time-Saving : Modern payroll software and automated systems reduce the time and effort spent on managing payroll, allowing companies to focus on productivity and growth. Talent Retention : Timely and accurate employee remuneration boosts job satisfaction and morale, reducing employee turnover and helping businesses retain top talent. Risk Mitigation : Entrusting payroll processes to dedicated professionals or automated systems reduces the chances of costly errors, ensuring accuracy and compliance. Company Reputation : Paying employees on time and accurately helps maintain a positive company image, which is crucial for attracting and retaining talent. Is Payroll a Human Resource or Accounting Function? Payroll touches both Human Resources (HR) and Accounting departments. HR's role involves overseeing the process of paying workers for their labor, ensuring employees receive salaries on time, and handling calculations, deductions, and withholdings. Employees typically approach HR regarding payment errors or queries. Accounting's role involves all financial transactions related to employee salaries, including recording expenses, tracking tax and insurance contributions, managing the payroll, performing audits, reconciling accounts, and preparing financial statements. The term "payroll" itself originated from medieval England, where stewards recorded employee names and salaries on "rolls" or parchments. With the advent of industrialization and income tax in 1799, more comprehensive systems became necessary for accurate documentation, solidifying the use of the term derived from "pay" (remunerating staff) and "roll" (periodical payment). Gross Pay vs. Net Pay: The Core Distinction Understanding the difference between gross pay and net pay is essential for both employees making financial decisions and employers managing payroll. Gross Pay : This is the total amount of money an employee earns before subtracting any payroll deductions and taxes . It's the figure indicated on the employment contract. Gross pay can be a fixed annual salary (e.g., $60,000 annually) or a multiplication of the hourly wage rate with the number of working hours (e.g., $20 per hour for 40 hours/week equals $800 weekly gross pay). While it won't appear in the bank account, it's the starting point for all calculations. Net Pay : This is the money an employee receives in their bank account after taxes, optional contributions, and other deductions have been subtracted . Net pay is more important than gross pay as it guides employees' financial activities. In rare cases, net pay may equal gross pay if income tax is negligible or the employee's salary falls below the government's taxation bracket. Common Deductions from Gross Pay : Taxes : Income taxes, federal income tax, state income tax, and other relevant national or local government taxes are subtracted. Insurance : Contributions to national health funds, disability, social security, health insurance, and unemployment insurance are common. Pension or Retirement Plan Contributions : A percentage of gross pay may be deducted for pension or retirement plans, with both employer and employee sometimes contributing. Bonus Payments : While appreciation for excellent work, bonuses and other incentives are often subject to taxation. Student Loan Payments : Some countries mandate that employers deduct student loan payments from employees' gross pay. Workers' Union Contributions : If applicable, these are also deducted. Key Differences Between Gross Pay and Net Pay : Gross pay is always higher than net pay . Gross pay accounts for all benefits paid by the employer, including overtime, holiday pay, and bonuses, while net income is exclusive of these benefits. Gross pay is derived from the cost to the company (CTC) , whereas net pay is what remains after subtracting taxes and deductions from gross income. Gross pay is the figure agreed upon in the employment contract and is typically the highest figure on a payslip, while net pay is the final, lower amount received in the bank account, often displayed in a bigger font on the payslip. Gross-Up : This refers to an amount an employer adds to an employee's payment to cover the income taxes the employee will owe for that payment. It helps employers relieve tax liability for things like bonuses or relocation expenses. For example, if $6,000 in relocation expenses is taxable, an employer might pay $9,000 to ensure the employee receives the full $6,000 benefit, with the extra $3,000 covering the tax. Preparing Your Payroll System Effective payroll begins with thorough preparation, including gathering employee information, choosing a suitable system, and establishing clear policies. 1. Gather Employee Information Before processing payroll, employers must collect crucial employee data: Personal Details : Name, address, and social security or insurance numbers. Banking Information : Bank account details for direct deposits. Work Information : Role, worked hours, and salary rates. Deduction Approvals : Official documentation for employee-approved deductions like medicare or retirement savings. Incentives : Information on applicable bonuses or commissions. 2. Choose a Payroll System The choice of payroll system should align with factors such as business size, growth, employee benefits, and local tax/federal laws. There are four distinct types of payroll systems: In-house Payroll : Managed internally by an employee or the business owner, suitable for small businesses with few employees and consistent working hours. Requires proper training in payroll practices and statutory laws. It can be economical for small businesses but may become challenging as the company grows. Outsourced Payroll Solutions : Involves hiring an external firm specializing in payroll processing. This option is convenient for companies of any size and ideal for those without an in-house payroll employee. These agencies offer services like time tracking and tax filing, ensuring accuracy and compliance from trained finance professionals. However, it means sharing employee data and potentially adjusting internal processes to match the agency's. Professionally Managed by Bookkeepers or CPAs : Employers can hire a professional bookkeeper or Certified Public Accountant (CPA) to manage payroll. This is popular among small and medium businesses lacking internal payroll resources, as these experts handle tax forms, prepare payroll, and offer valuable insights. Software-Managed / Cloud-based Payroll : Increasingly popular, these systems are cloud-based, cost-effective, easy to use, and efficient. Payroll software, like Workpay, automates the processing, reduces human error, and generates comprehensive payroll reports and pay stubs. Data entry, time tracking, tax filing, calculations, and recordkeeping are all managed in the cloud. 3. Establish a Payroll Policy A defined payroll policy provides guidelines and regulations for how payroll processing should be carried out, ensuring transparency and that employees understand their rights. Key elements include: Pay Dates : Dictates the length of the pay period (e.g., weekly, biweekly, monthly) and when employees should expect their salaries. Payment Methods : Specifies how employees will receive their salaries (e.g., direct deposits, paychecks, mobile wallets). Deductions : Outlines procedures for necessary deductions such as taxes and insurance, along with relevant regulations. Benefits : Clearly states any employee benefits like overtime, tax exemptions, and leave payments. Calculating Payroll: A Step-by-Step Guide Once preparation is complete, the next crucial step is calculating each employee's salary accurately. 1. Calculate Gross Pay : Salaried Employees : Divide the annual salary by the stipulated pay periods. For instance, an $84,000 annual salary paid monthly results in a $7,000 monthly gross pay. Hourly Employees : Multiply the agreed hourly rate by the total number of hours worked in a given period. For example, $25 per hour for 40 hours a week yields a $1,000 weekly gross pay. 2. Account for All Mandatory and Voluntary Deductions : Reference each employee's tax details and review the country's laws regarding tax withholdings. Mandatory Deductions : These vary by country but commonly include income tax, social security contributions, health care premiums, and retirement plan payments. Voluntary Deductions : These depend on employee preference and require their consent, such as additional retirement savings or union contributions. Special Considerations : Overtime : Money paid for extra hours worked, usually calculated separately and applicable only to eligible employees. Incentives : Bonuses, allowances, commissions, and other benefits that vary by employer. PTO Compensation : Paid leaves like holidays, vacations, sick leave, parental leave, maternity leave, and annual leave. Employee Contributions to Social Securities’ Funds : Mandatory contributions for pension, health, housing, or disability insurance, remitted to the government. 3. Calculate Net Pay : Sum up all mandatory and voluntary deductions. Subtract the total deductions from the gross pay to arrive at the employee's net income. The formula is: Net Pay = Gross Pay - Payroll Deductions . Withholding Calculation Methods : Percentage Method : Withholding taxes based on predetermined percentage rates set by relevant authorities. Wage Bracket Method : Finds its basis on an employee's income level. Using a payroll calculator or automated payroll software can simplify calculations and ensure compliance with tax laws and regulations. The Payroll Accounting Process in Africa Payroll accounting is the structured recording and tracking of financial transactions related to employee compensation , sitting at the intersection of human resources, finance, and compliance. In Africa, where businesses are rapidly expanding, accurate payroll accounting forms the backbone of reliable financial reporting. What Payroll Accounting Involves : Employee's Gross Pay : Includes base salary, overtime pay, bonuses, and commissions. Payroll Deductions : Mandatory withholdings like income tax and voluntary deductions such as retirement plan contributions or life insurance. Payroll Liabilities : Employer's obligations, including insurance contributions and health insurance premiums. Direct Labor and Employee Benefits : Costs associated with staff output and welfare. Payroll Tax : State income tax, federal income tax, and related withholdings based on local tax laws and regulations. Accuracy in payroll accounting is crucial for maintaining clean financial records, generating timely financial statements, and complying with evolving tax rules. The Payroll Accounting Process : Initial recordings of employee wages and benefits. Staff payment entries into the general ledger and payroll journal. Tax withholdings and compliance with state and federal tax laws. Direct deposit or other payment methods (e.g., manual payments, mobile money). Reconciliation of bank statements and posting to the balance sheet. Review of the company’s chart of accounts to categorize salary payments as operational expenses or cost of goods sold. These steps can be complex and time-consuming when performed manually, especially across multiple regions with differing payroll cycles and regulations. Types of Payroll Accounting : Accrual Payroll Accounting : Recognizes expenses in the accounting period when employees earn them, not when the cash is actually disbursed. Cash Payroll Accounting : Records expenses only when cash is disbursed. Manual vs. Automated Payroll Systems : Manual systems carry higher risks of errors and non-compliance, whereas automated systems or payroll accounting software offer greater accuracy and real-time processing capabilities. Challenges with Traditional Payroll Operations in Africa : Managing salary disbursements in Africa presents unique challenges due to constantly changing tax rates, fragmented tax regulations, variations in minimum wage and benefits, and the burden of tracking diverse expenses and government contributions. Many small businesses still rely on spreadsheets or outdated tools that often don't integrate with their accounting software, leading to inconsistent data, missed deductions, and reporting delays. Processing and Managing Payroll with Modern Solutions Once calculations are accurate, the final stage involves processing and disbursing payments, followed by reporting and record-keeping. 1. Approve Payroll Before disbursing payments, companies must thoroughly review all calculations to prevent errors in employee payments. 2. Pay Employees Once verified and submitted, employees can be paid through various methods, including direct deposits, cash, mobile wallets, checks, prepaid cards, or pay cards. 3. Report and Update Payroll Records After payments are made, it's essential to update payroll records and review payroll data to generate reports for actionable insights and to track tax contributions. 4. Prepare Employee Payslips Payslips are crucial documents that outline an employee's pay for a given period, detailing all deductions, benefits, and net income, ensuring transparency and accuracy. Payroll software can automate payslip generation, ensuring correct information. Processing Tools and Workpay's Role Modern processing tools connect to banks and other payment systems, simplifying the disbursement of salaries. Workpay is an HR and Payroll software company that offers a comprehensive automated system designed to streamline various tasks , from calculation, tax withholding, and deductions to generating paychecks and direct deposits. Workpay specializes in solutions for businesses across Africa. How Workpay Enhances the Payroll Accounting Process in Africa : End-to-End Salary Disbursement Management : Automates the entire payment cycle, from calculating an employee’s gross pay to submitting tax obligations, minimizing input from HR or finance. Integrated System : Cloud-based HR and payroll software seamlessly integrates with major accounting software like QuickBooks and Xero, eliminating redundant entries and ensuring clean financial statements. Real-Time Reporting and Compliance : Ensures full tax compliance with federal and state income tax filings. Tailored dashboards allow real-time tracking of overtime pay, insurance contributions, and tax withholdings per employee. Direct Deposit and Employee Access : Employees receive payments via direct deposit and can access payslips, benefit summaries, and retirement plan contributions through a self-service portal. Workpay serves a wide range of global and African businesses, from startups to multinationals, helping HR and finance teams align on multi-country salary payment operations, tracking salaries and bonuses, auto-calculating tax withholdings and health insurance, managing statutory obligations, maintaining consistent financial tracking for audit readiness, and generating clean payroll data. By automating compliance and streamlining financial reporting, Workpay aims to enhance employee well-being through timely, accurate payments. Finally, employers should prioritize secure log-in procedures for payroll systems, using passwords, usernames, and multi-factor authentication to protect sensitive information. Staying updated with ever-changing payroll laws and regulations is also crucial. With the right tools and knowledge, managing payroll can be a seamless and efficient process for businesses in Africa. ‍

title: Why Scaling Makes Microservices Testing Exponentially Harder
summary: The logical assumption that testing will get easier if your engineering team scales along with your microservices growth is completely wrong.
body_text: The logical assumption that testing will get easier if your engineering team scales along with your microservices growth is completely wrong. I was chatting with a VP of engineering last week who made an observation that stuck with me: “When we had five microservices, testing was actually easier than our old monolith . At 50 services, it’s become our biggest bottleneck.” This isn’t uncommon. Most teams experience a honeymoon period with microservices where testing feels manageable, even elegant. Then something shifts. What was once a competitive advantage becomes a drag on velocity. The question is: Why does microservices testing difficulty seem to grow exponentially, rather than linearly? The Deceptive Early Days In the beginning, microservices testing feels like a breath of fresh air. You’ve got clean service boundaries and focused test suites, and each team can move independently. Testing a payment service? Spin up the service, mock the user service and you’re done. Simple. This early success creates a reasonable assumption that testing complexity will scale proportionally with the number of services and developers. After all, if each service can be tested in isolation and you’re growing your engineering team alongside your services, why wouldn’t the testing effort scale linearly? It’s a logical assumption. And it’s completely wrong. The Hidden Exponential Forces The reality is that testing complexity in microservices grows exponentially due to several compounding factors that aren’t obvious when you’re starting out. Integration Points Multiply Rapidly With five services, you might have eight or 10 integration points to test. But integration points don’t scale linearly — they scale based on the interconnectedness of your system. Source: Signadot . Think about it: Each service doesn’t just call one other service. A typical microservice might integrate with four to six other services — authentication, logging, data storage, notification services, plus two or three business logic services. As your architecture grows, services become more interconnected, not less. That order service doesn’t just talk to inventory; it also hits payment processing, user management, shipping, analytics and audit logging. The result? Integration points grow much faster than the number of services, creating a web of dependencies that must be validated. Each new service doesn’t just add its own test requirements. It potentially interacts with multiple existing services, creating a web of dependencies that must be validated. What started as simple point-to-point testing becomes a complex and sprawling validation challenge . Mock Maintenance Becomes Unsustainable Mocking strategies that work beautifully at a small scale become maintenance disasters at a large scale. One API change can require updating dozens of mocks across different codebases, owned by different teams. A platform engineering director recently told me: “We calculated that our teams spend 40% of their testing time just maintaining mocks.” Environment Multiplication Spirals Out of Control With five services, maintaining three to four test environments per team feels reasonable. Scale to 50 services across 15 teams, and suddenly you need 45-60 environments. The infrastructure costs and operational complexity become staggering. One of our customers was spending $2 million annually just on pre-production environments before it rethought its approach. The ops team was spending more time maintaining test infrastructure than building new capabilities. This is precisely the million-dollar problem of slow microservices testing that organizations face as they scale beyond a handful of services. Amplifying the Staging Bottleneck Perhaps the most painful scaling challenge is what happens to shared staging environments. With a few services, staging works reasonably well. Multiple teams can coordinate deployments, and when something breaks, the culprit is usually obvious. But as you add services and teams, staging becomes either a traffic jam or a free-for-all — and both are disastrous. Source: Signadot. Option 1: Exclusive Access Queuing Some organizations implement strict scheduling where teams get exclusive staging access. I’ve seen teams wait eight or more hours for their turn, with elaborate coordination systems — Slackbots, deployment calendars and other mechanisms — to manage the queue. The math here is brutal. If you have 20 teams each needing staging access twice per week, and each testing session takes two hours, you need 80 hours of staging time weekly. But you only have 40 hours (one environment, Monday through Friday). At an average fully loaded engineering cost of $150 per hour, those wait times translate to thousands of dollars in lost productivity weekly. One organization we work with calculated it was burning $400,000 annually just on engineers waiting for staging access. Option 2: Shared Access Chaos More commonly, teams share staging concurrently without coordination. No waiting, but now multiple teams are deploying and testing simultaneously. Test failures become meaningless — is it your code or someone else’s deployment that broke the flow? This creates a perverse outcome: Developers lose trust in test results and start ignoring failures, assuming they’re environment-related. Teams push code to production despite failing tests, leading to production incidents. The very environment meant to catch bugs before production becomes a source of false confidence. This is exactly why staging doesn’t scale for microservice testing — the fundamental assumptions break down as teams and services multiply. When Teams Start Gaming the System As testing becomes more painful, teams begin developing workarounds that make the underlying problems worse: Batching changes: Instead of testing individual features, teams batch multiple changes together to “optimize” staging time. This makes debugging exponentially harder when something breaks. Testing shortcuts: Teams skip integration tests and hope for the best, or test only the “happy path” to save time. Quality inevitably suffers. Environment hoarding: Teams start reserving staging environments longer than needed, creating artificial scarcity. Parallel development stalls: Teams start coordinating their development cycles to avoid staging conflicts, destroying the independence that microservices promised. Breaking the Exponential Curve The teams that successfully scale microservices testing have figured out how to break this exponential curve. They’ve moved away from trying to duplicate production environments for testing and are instead focused on creating isolated slices of their production-like environment. Instead of spinning up 50 services for every test scenario, they spin up only the two or three services being modified and route test traffic to production-like versions of everything else. This smart ephemeral environment approach caps the complexity growth while maintaining high-fidelity testing. Here’s how this breaks each of the exponential scaling problems: Integration complexity: Instead of testing 200+ integration points, you test only the four to six integration points for your modified services against real dependencies. Mock maintenance: No mocks needed — your changes test against actual production-like services, eliminating maintenance overhead. Environment multiplication: One shared baseline environment supports unlimited isolated testing through request-level routing, dramatically reducing infrastructure costs . Staging bottlenecks: Every developer gets their own isolated testing environment instantly, with no queuing and no interference from other teams’ changes. One customer explained it perfectly: “We stopped trying to recreate the entire world for every test. Instead, we create a small bubble of change and test how it interacts with the real world.” The Path Forward Microservices testing doesn’t have to become exponentially complex as you scale. The key is recognizing early that traditional testing approaches don’t scale beyond 10-15 services and adopting testing that grows linearly with your architecture. At Signadot, we’ve built a platform that enables sandbox environments for exactly this problem — allowing teams to test individual changes against production-like dependencies without the exponential complexity. If you’re hitting the testing wall, try it for free and see how linear scaling changes everything. title: Evotec SE: H1 2025 results: Strong progress on strategy execution
summary: Evotec SE today announced financial results for H1 2025, demonstrating clear progress in the implementation of its new strategy for sustainable and profitable growth; highlighting Just – Evotec Biologics’ strong growth as it transitions to an asset-lighter model. body_text: Evotec SE reports H1 2025 results: Strong progress on strategy execution Strategy for sustainable profitable growth progressing as planned with improving revenue mix and ahead-of-plan cost reductions Reporting segment formerly known as Shared R&D renamed to Discovery & Preclinical Development (“D&PD”) to better reflect strategic focus Group revenues of € 371.2 m (-5%); D&PD (-11%) continues to see soft demand; Just – Evotec Biologics (“JEB”; +16%) exceeding expectations driven by broadened customer base Key progress in collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb (“BMS”) on targeted protein degradation and neuroscience Evolution of strategic partnership with Sandoz announced on 30 July Hamburg, Germany, 13 August 2025: Evotec SE (Frankfurt Stock Exchange: EVT, MDAX/TecDAX, Prime Standard, ISIN: DE0005664809, WKN 566480; NASDAQ: EVO) today announced financial results for H1 2025, demonstrating clear progress in the implementation of its new strategy for sustainable and profitable growth; highlighting Just – Evotec Biologics’ strong growth as it transitions to an asset-lighter model. Dr Christian Wojczewski, Chief Executive Officer of Evotec, said: “We are firmly on track with the execution of our strategy: Evotec is making meaningful strides toward sustainable and profitable growth. JEB maintained its strong growth trajectory with first half revenues in excess of € 100 m, and the evolution of our strategic partnership with Sandoz is testament to its bright future as a scalable technology provider with a more capital-efficient model. Our base business in D&PD continues to face soft demand, but we see strong progress in core collaborations and are systematically expanding our platform technologies, such as our Molecular Patient Database. I am confident that our unrelenting focus on technology and science leadership will continue to drive tangible impact in the future”. title: Fluent, Inc. Adds Authentic Brands Group to Partner Network, Powering Post-Purchase Monetization Across Brand Portfolio
summary: Fluent expands its partnership with Authentic Brands Group, adding Reebok, Vince Camuto, Champion, and more to its commerce media network to boost post-purchase monetization.
body_text: NEW YORK, August 14, 2025 ( GLOBE NEWSWIRE ) — Fluent, Inc. (NASDAQ: FLNT), a leader in commerce media, today announced an expanded partnership with Authentic Brands Group (Authentic) , bringing a portfolio of iconic brands into Fluent’s growing network of commerce media partners – further reinforcing its position as a trusted post-purchase monetization partner to leading retailers. Authentic is the world’s leading sports, lifestyle, and entertainment brand owner, with a portfolio that generates more than $32 billion in global annual retail sales. The partnership follows successful campaign launches across several of Authentic’s owned and licensed brands, including Eddie Bauer, Nautica, Lucky Brand, and Aéropostale. Now, through a broader agreement, Fluent will support post-purchase monetization for additional brands such as Reebok, Vince Camuto, Volcom, Champion, RVCA, DC Shoes, and more— with the goal of adding millions of annual transactions to Fluent’s growing commerce media partner network. “Our partnership with Authentic represents a major step forward in Fluent’s mission to build a robust, high-performance commerce media network,” said Tim Lukens, President of Commerce Media Solutions at Fluent . “With Authentic’s globally recognized portfolio and massive retail reach, we’re unlocking premium ad inventory for brands — while helping Authentic drive new revenue streams and elevate the customer experience at checkout.” By integrating Fluent’s post-purchase ad technology, Authentic’s retail partners can deliver personalized, non-endemic offers that drive incremental revenue without disrupting the consumer journey—further deepening brand loyalty while creating performance-driven touchpoints for advertisers. "Fluent has proven to be a strong partner in helping us unlock incremental value across our portfolio,” said Adam Kronengold, Chief Digital Officer at Authentic Brands Group . “Their data-driven approach and commerce media expertise will continue to help us drive new revenue while enhancing the customer experience with relevant and engaging content at the moment of transaction.” This portfolio-level partnership highlights Fluent’s value as a strategic monetization partner to some of the most influential players in retail. To learn more about Fluent’s post-purchase monetization solutions and partner network, visit https://fluentco.com/for-partners/. About Fluent, Inc. Fluent, Inc. (NASDAQ: FLNT) is a commerce media solutions provider connecting top-tier brands with highly engaged consumers. Leveraging exclusive ad inventory, robust first-party data, privacy-first infrastructure, and proprietary machine learning, Fluent unlocks additional revenue streams for partners and empowers advertisers to acquire their most valuable customers at scale. Founded in 2010, Fluent uses its deep expertise in performance marketing to drive monetization and increase engagement at key touchpoints across the customer journey. For more insights, visit https://www.fluentco.com .
